body:
## Phase 1 note — leave an open, de-plan-ized **connect-policy** seam (don't fork for cloud)

Recording a design constraint surfaced while reviewing the open/closed boundary for this epic.

**Conclusion:** everything in this epic (D1–D8, all phases) is **open-core runtime mechanism** — it all lands in framework, nothing is EE/closed. ADR-0062's Non-goals already scope out "multi-tenant credential vaulting beyond the SecretBinder seam", so the closed pieces (KMS `SecretBinder` impl, AI introspection, multi-tenant egress/quota governance) live in the cloud repo **on top of** the seams this epic exposes — not in here.

**But** the multi-tenant host (shared-container cloud) needs to be able to *disable* external-datasource connect (SSRF / egress isolation) while self-hosted single-env runs it on by default. So Phase 1's `DatasourceConnectionService` must consult an **injectable connect policy** before building/registering a driver — not hard-code "always connect".

Concretely, when implementing **D1/D5**:
- Add an injectable `DatasourceConnectPolicy` (or fold it into the D5 connect-error/lifecycle hook) consulted **before** connect, alongside the existing D2 gate (`external` / routed / `autoConnect:true`).
- **Open-core default impl = allow** (subject to D2) → self-host works out of the box, **de-plan-ized**, no plan coupling in framework.
- The host can bind a stricter policy. Cloud will bind one that checks `sys_environment.plan` + egress allow-list + per-tenant quota and **fail-closes** on the shared runtime — that impl stays in the cloud repo.

Net: framework gains *one open policy interface + a permissive default*. Same single connect path for code- and runtime-origin (D1) — the host injects a stricter policy, we do **not** fork a second connect path for cloud. No cloud-side ADR needed; cloud's policy reuses the existing plan-gating mechanism (the same place that gates the AI authoring assistant today).
